subproblem.title: Transport of mu_V-integrals over B_s(xi) to the parameter domain of the C^1 graph
subproblem.statement:
Let n, l be natural numbers, U a subset of R^(n+l), V = v(M, theta) a rectifiable n-varifold in U (RectifiableVarifold n l U) with weight mu_V and support Sigma := V.support, xi in R^(n+l), s, R reals with s <= R, Q a linear isometry equivalence of R^(n+l), and u : R^n -> R^l of class C^1 on the open ball Bo^n_R(0). Assume Q(Sigma - xi) cap Bo_R(0) = graph_{Bo^n_R(0)} u cap Bo_R(0) and that mu_V restricted to Bo_s(xi) equals H^n restricted to Sigma cap Bo_s(xi) (H^n = muHE[n]). Let D_s := {x in Bo^n_R(0) : |(x, u(x))| < s} and J(P) := sqrt(det(delta_{ab} +

)_{a,b}). Then for every function f : R^(n+l) -> R (no measurability or integrability assumed; Bochner integrals), the integral over Bo_s(xi) of f d mu_V equals the integral over D_s, with respect to Lebesgue measure, of J(Du(x)) f(xi + Q^{-1}(x, u(x))) dx.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (ξ : Amb n ℓ) (s R : ℝ) (Q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (u : Rn n → Rn ℓ), s ≤ R → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 u (ball 0 R) → Q '' ((fun x => x - ξ) '' V.support) ∩ ball 0 R = graphOver u (ball 0 R) ∩ ball 0 R → V.weight.restrict (ball ξ s) = (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)).restrict (V.support ∩ ball ξ s) → ∀ f : Amb n ℓ → ℝ, ∫ y in ball ξ s, f y ∂V.weight = ∫ x in {x : Rn n | x ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) R ∧ ‖graphPoint x (u x)‖ < s}, Real.sqrt (Matrix.det ((1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + Matrix.of fun a b : Fin n => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ u x (EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ))) (fderiv ℝ u x (EuclideanSpace.single b (1 : ℝ))))) * f (ξ + Q.symm (graphPoint x (u x)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the transport chain '(iii), then (Iso), then (Area)' of Steps 6 and 7 of the parent proof: integral over Bo_s(xi) of k d mu_V = integral over Sigma cap Bo_s(xi) of k dH^n = integral over D_s of k(xi + Q^{-1} G(x)) J(Du(x)) dx. The (Area) step uses the sibling dohr_vel_graph_area_formula instead of simongmt's area formula (not reachable from the frozen imports); everything else is in the frozen imports. Notation: G(x) := graphPoint x (u x), Phi(x) := xi + Q^{-1}(G x), T(y) := Q(y - xi), A(z) := xi + Q^{-1} z.

1. Reduction to H^n. The integral over Bo_s(xi) of f d mu_V is the integral of f against mu_V restricted to Bo_s(xi); by the measure hypothesis it equals the integral over Sigma cap Bo_s(xi) of f dH^n (rewrite the measure; no property of f is used).
2. D_s is open. u is differentiable, hence continuous, on the open ball Bo^n_R(0) (ContDiffOn of order 1), graphPoint is a continuous linear function of the pair, so G is continuous on Bo^n_R(0) and D_s = Bo^n_R(0) cap G^{-1}(Bo_s(0)) is open (ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage). Also D_s is contained in Bo^n_R(0), so u is C^1 on D_s.
3. Sigma cap Bo_s(xi) = Phi(D_s). We have |T y| = |y - xi| and Q^{-1}(T y) = y - xi. (subset) If y is in Sigma cap Bo_s(xi), then T y lies in Q(Sigma - xi) and |T y| < s <= R, so T y lies in Q(Sigma - xi) cap Bo_R(0) = graph cap Bo_R(0): T y = G(x) for some x in Bo^n_R(0); |G x| = |T y| < s gives x in D_s, and Phi(x) = xi + Q^{-1}(T y) = y. (superset) If x is in D_s then |G x| < s <= R, so G x lies in graph cap Bo_R(0) = Q(Sigma - xi) cap Bo_R(0), i.e. G x = Q(y - xi) with y in Sigma; then Phi(x) = y is in Sigma and |Phi(x) - xi| = |G x| < s.
4. Phi is continuous on D_s (step 2; A is continuous) and injective (Phi x = Phi x' gives G x = G x', and the first n coordinates give x = x'). A is an isometry of R^(n+l).
5. Set-level area formula. For every measurable B contained in D_s: Phi(B) = A(G(B)), so H^n(Phi B) = H^n(G B) (isometry invariance of muHE[n], Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) = integral over B of J(Du(x)) dx (sibling dohr_vel_graph_area_formula with D := D_s, open by step 2, and u C^1 on D_s).
6. The density x -> J(Du(x)) is Borel measurable (fderiv of any function is measurable, measurable_fderiv; J is continuous) and nonnegative.
7. Measure identity. The restriction e of Phi to the subtype D_s is a measurable embedding (ContinuousOn.measurableEmbedding: D_s is Borel, Phi continuous and injective on D_s, the spaces are Polish). Let nu be the pullback to the subtype D_s (Measure.comap Subtype.val) of Lebesgue measure with density J(Du). For measurable t, (Measure.map e nu)(t) = nu(e^{-1} t) = (Lebesgue with density J(Du))(B_t), where B_t := Subtype.val(e^{-1} t) is a measurable subset of D_s; by withDensity_apply and step 5 this equals H^n(Phi(B_t)) = H^n(t cap Phi(D_s)). Hence Measure.map e nu = H^n restricted to Phi(D_s).
8. Conclusion for arbitrary f. Using steps 1 and 3, then step 7: integral over Sigma cap Bo_s(xi) of f dH^n = integral over Phi(D_s) of f dH^n = integral of f d(Measure.map e nu) = integral of f o e d nu (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map, valid for every f) = integral over D_s of f o Phi with respect to Lebesgue measure with density J(Du) (the subtype inclusion is a measurable embedding and map_comap_subtype_coe) = integral over D_s of J(Du(x)) f(Phi(x)) dx (setIntegral_withDensity_eq_setIntegral_smul with the measurable density of step 6, and J >= 0).

proof_key_steps: rewrite mu_V restricted to Bo_s(xi) as H^n restricted to Sigma cap Bo_s(xi)
D_s is open; Sigma cap Bo_s(xi) = Phi(D_s) with Phi(x) = xi + Q^{-1}(x, u(x)); Phi continuous and injective on D_s
set-level formula H^n(Phi B) = integral_B J(Du) from isometry invariance and dohr_vel_graph_area_formula
Phi restricted to D_s is a measurable embedding; its pushforward of J(Du) dx on D_s is H^n restricted to Phi(D_s)
integral transport through the measurable embedding holds for every f, giving the Bochner identity
